PDF 83 lines 26-27 grant the permission 'provided' the other Main has more than one parameter or a single non-string[] parameter, the same word lines 23-24 use for the necessary condition on overloads, so static double Main(string[]) beside static void Main() is not permitted at ISO-1. But that condition is not a syntax rule or a shall, shall not, error or warning requirement, so its violation is undefined behavior with no diagnostic required (PDF 17 lines 17-20, 33-35), and even read as ill formed, lines 38-40 let a compiler build it after a diagnostic, which csc's CS0028 warning supplies. No conforming ISO-1 compiler can be shown wrong for accepting it, so the probes' Expected: reject has no basis and no test should be published; the sufficient-permission reading would give NO-DIFFERENCE, also with no test.

The member set is stated without qualification (PDF 87 line 34), invocation is defined with no Invoke member (PDF 157 lines 25-37; PDF 316 lines 25-28), and the edition incorporates only CLI Partition IV, not the Partition II delegate layout that requires Invoke (PDF 19 lines 9-10), so Invoke is not a 1st-edition member. But PDF 17 lines 36-38 let an implementation provide additional methods that change no strictly conforming program, so a compiler that accepts d.Invoke(7) and one that rejects it both conform at ISO-1. No test can expect either outcome; the 7th-edition Invoke rules (E7-4-8-delegate-invoke-method, -return-type, -parameters, -equivalence) belong to a later level and should not run at ISO-1.

At ISO-1, a reference to a type's private member made in that type's own attribute section or class-base, outside its body braces, is a compile-time error: [ImprintAttribute(Casket.Code)] class Casket { private const int Code = 31; } and class Vessel : Vessel.ISeal { private interface ISeal {} } are rejected, while the same reference inside the body, or with the member made public, compiles and prints OK 0.

At ISO-1, [ImprintAttribute(Casket.Code)] class Casket { private const int Code = 31; } and class Vessel : Vessel.ISeal { private interface ISeal {} } are compile-time errors; the same reference on a member inside the body, or with the member made public, compiles and prints OK 0.

At ISO-1, [ImprintAttribute(Bough.Code)] class Grove { private const int Code = 43; } class Bough : Grove {} is a compile-time error, since Grove's own attribute is outside Grove's body; the same reference on a member inside Grove's body compiles.

At ISO-1, [ImprintAttribute(Timber.Code)] class Shoot : Timber {} where Timber declares protected const int Code is a compile-time error, whether Timber is in a referenced library or in the same program; the same access on a member inside Shoot's body compiles.

At ISO-1, with public class Timber { protected internal const int Code = 47; } in a referenced library, the consumer's [ImprintAttribute(Timber.Code)] class Shoot : Timber {} is a compile-time error, since the attribute is outside both the library's text and Shoot's body; the same access on a member inside Shoot's body compiles.
